extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and PTAB bar (attorneys/agents appearing before the PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Slide-deck guidance from PTAB judges covering recent changes to PTAB practice, procedures for Director review after Arthrex, fast-track appeals pilots, the Motion to Amend (MTA) pilot, discretion to deny institution (§314(a)/§325(d)), and related rulemaking and guidance. Intended to guide practitioners in filing, responding, and seeking review in AIA and ex parte matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised claim construction standard (Nov. 2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised claim construction standard used in AIA proceedings (Nov. 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a change to the way claims are construed in AIA trials; practitioners should apply the November 2018 standard when drafting petitions, responses, and institution analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Operating Procedures (Sept. 2018) including SOP 1 (paneling) and SOP 2 (two new processes to designate decisions precedential or informative, including POP review on rehearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOP 1 governs how panels are constituted; SOP 2 establishes processes for designating decisions as precedential or informative and includes POP review on rehearing. Practitioners should be aware of paneling practices and that designation processes may affect reliance on decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated precedential and informative decisions (topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated precedential and informative decisions cover issues such as real parties-in-interest; joinder; printed publications; and discretionary denials of institution under 35 U.S.C. § 314(a) and § 325(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These designated decisions provide binding or persuasive guidance on recurring legal issues—counsel should consult them when evaluating institution risk, joinder strategy, and evidentiary sufficiency for printed publications and real-party-in-interest inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Amend practice pilot program (March 2019 onward)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion to amend practice pilot program initiated in March 2019 and extended until September 16, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pilot alters how motions to amend (MTAs) are handled in AIA trials; practitioners should follow pilot procedures (see separate MTA Pilot entries) and monitor extensions/updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTA Pilot — PO options and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: MTA Pilot program provides patent owner (PO) two options: (1) request preliminary guidance (PG) from the Board on its MTA (Board will provide PG within 4 weeks of due date for Opp. to MTA if requested); (2) file a revised MTA after receiving petitioner's opposition and/or Board's PG. Option 1 is not a predicate for Option 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PO requests PG, Board will issue PG within four weeks of the opposition due date. Based on the petitioner's opposition and/or PG, the PO may file a reply to the opposition and PG, file a revised MTA, or do nothing (Board treats it like a normal MTA). PO electing Option 1 need not be precluded from Option 2, but Option 1 is not a prerequisite for Option 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTA Pilot — outcomes/statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: MTA Pilot statistics (Mar. 15, 2019 to Aug. 31, 2021): POs file MTAs in about same % of cases as before (~10%); ~164 MTAs qualifying for pilot filed; PTAB decided ~78 MTAs on merits in FWD; POs elected one or both pilot options in vast majority of cases; POs filing MTAs under pilot more likely to have MTAs granted for at least one substitute claim (pre-pilot = 14% granted or granted in part; pilot overall = 27% granted or granted in part).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data indicate improved grant rates for MTAs under the pilot. Practitioners should consider pilot procedures to increase likelihood of obtaining substitute claims and track PTAB's published statistics for updated results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice re: reissue and reexamination options (Apr. 2019)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice explaining reissue and reexamination options (April 2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office published guidance outlining when patentees might pursue reissue or reexamination instead of, or in addition to, AIA proceedings. Counsel should consider these options when formulating remediation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2019 revised patent subject matter eligibility guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: 2019 revised patent subject matter eligibility guidance impacting ex parte appeals and AIA cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to subject matter eligibility guidance affect both ex parte and AIA practice; practitioners should apply the revised guidance in claim drafting, petitioning, and appeal strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updates to Trial Practice Guide (Nov. 2019 consolidation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Updates to the Trial Practice Guide consolidated in Nov. 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The consolidated Trial Practice Guide summarizes procedural expectations and practice points for trials; counsel should consult the updated guide for filing requirements, briefing conventions, and trial practice norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking on AIA trial institution and responsive briefing (Dec. 2020)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking on AIA trial institution and responsive briefing published Dec. 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pending/implemented rule changes alter institution analyses and responsive briefing requirements; practitioners should verify current rules and adapt petitions and responses accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking to allocate burdens of persuasion on motions to amend (Dec. 2020)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking to allocate burdens of persuasion on motions to amend in AIA trial proceedings (Dec. 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes address who bears the persuasion burden on MTAs. Counsel should incorporate the new burden allocation into MTA strategy and supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director memoranda clarifying §311(b) and applicant-admitted prior art (Aug. 2020)
rubrics_metrics.description: Director issued a memorandum clarifying interpretation of § 311(b) in relation to applicant admitted prior art (Aug. 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This memorandum provides the Office's approach to petitions that raise claims or art tied to applicant admissions—practitioners should consider its effect when selecting grounds and framing petitionable art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director memorandum on indefiniteness approach in AIA proceedings (Jan. 2021)
rubrics_metrics.description: Director issued a memorandum clarifying approach to indefiniteness in AIA proceedings (Jan. 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum explains how indefiniteness challenges are treated in AIA trials; petitioners and patent owners should tailor indefiniteness arguments to the Office's stated approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary denials — §314(a), §325(d), and serial/parallel considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Current discretionary-denial considerations include serial/parallel petitions, proceedings in other tribunals, and §325(d) (relating to previously considered art/arguments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deciding whether to institute, the Board may exercise discretion based on whether claims were previously challenged (serial petitions), whether multiple petitions are filed around the same time, and whether the patent has been subject to other tribunal proceedings. Petitioners should anticipate discretionary-denial risks when filing follow-on petitions or petitions overlapping with district court/ITC activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFC on discretion to institute AIA trials — institution considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for Comments (Oct. 2020) sought input on whether to promulgate rules with case-specific analyses for deciding whether to institute a trial for (1) petitions on claims previously challenged in another petition; (2) more than one petition filed at/about same time on same patent; (3) petitions on patents subject to U.S. district court or ITC proceedings; and (4) any other considerations regarding discretion to institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RFC solicited stakeholder views on formalizing institution-discretion analyses. Practitioners should review the Executive Summary and comments (822 comments received) to understand stakeholder perspectives and possible future rulemaking affecting institution discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arthrex remedial authority — Director review of final PTAB decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: United States v. Arthrex held that the Director “may review final PTAB decisions and, upon review, may issue decisions himself on behalf of the Board.” The remedy permits Director review to address the Appointments Clause issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arthrex's remedy authorizes Director review of final PTAB decisions. Parties should be aware that Director review can change the landscape of final decisions and that implementation is via an interim procedure described by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Director review — initiation, scope, and who may request
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim procedure: Director review may be initiated sua sponte by the Director or requested by a party to a PTAB proceeding. Only a party to a case may submit a request for Director review; third-party requests are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director review can be initiated by the Director on his own or by a party to the case. Third parties cannot request Director review. Parties should plan their post-decision strategy knowing that Director review may be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — scope and review standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director’s review may address any issue, including issues of fact and issues of law, and will be de novo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director review is not limited to legal questions; factual findings may be revisited de novo. Parties requesting Director review should present comprehensive arguments and, where appropriate, offer factual clarification or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — procedural requirements and timing (37 C.F.R. 42.71(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: To request Director review of a final written decision in an inter partes review or post-grant review, a party must concurrently (1) file a request for rehearing by the Director of a PTAB decision and (2) submit a notification of that request by email to Director_PTABDecision_Review@uspto.gov, copying counsel. A request for rehearing by the Director must satisfy timing of 37 C.F.R. 42.71(d) — must be filed within 30 days of entry of a final written decision or a decision on rehearing by a PTAB panel. A timely request for rehearing by the Director will be considered a request under 37 C.F.R. 90.3(b) and will reset the time for appeal or civil action as set forth in that rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must follow the concurrent filing + email-notification process and comply with the 30-day deadline. If both Director review and panel rehearing are requested together or in the alternative, the Office will treat the filings as a request for Director review. Filing deadlines may be extended for good cause if requested before the due date; parties whose rehearing deadlines expired at time Arthrex issued may request a waiver if done before the notice-of-appeal due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — interim procedural features (fees, POP, future changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Precedential Opinion Panel (POP) process remains in effect presently, though the Office will review POP in view of Director review. During implementation of the interim procedure, the USPTO will not charge a fee. The current process is envisioned as interim and may change based on public input and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee currently for Director review; POP remains but may be reconsidered. The Office welcomes suggestions (Director_Review_Suggestions@uspto.gov) and may update procedures—parties should monitor announcements and may provide feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — restrictions on concurrent requests
rubrics_metrics.description: After a panel issues a final written decision, a party may request either Director review or rehearing by the original PTAB panel, but may not request both. If the panel grants rehearing, a party may subsequently request Director review of that decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategically, parties must choose between panel rehearing and Director review initially; however, a later Director review may be sought if the panel grants rehearing. If both are filed together or in the alternative, it will be treated as Director review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-Track Appeals Pilot Program — eligibility and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Fast-track appeals pilot: expedited decisions for ex parte appeals; running until July 2, 2022; requires petition and $420 fee; six-month pendency goal; 125-granted-petition limit per quarter (500 total); hearings permitted, with some restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To use the pilot, file a petition and pay the fee; note the cap on granted petitions per quarter and pendency goal. Hearings may be allowed subject to restrictions. Practitioners should assess whether an appeal qualifies and weigh the fee and timing benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: COVID Fast-Track Appeals Pilot (COVID-related appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expedited decisions for ex parte appeals related to COVID-19; running until April 15, 2022; requires petition but no fee; six-month pendency goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee for COVID-related pilot but petition required. Use when appeal involves COVID-19-related technologies or matters and track the program expiration date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and resource points for PTAB practice changes
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB provides webpages, Q&As, and contact emails: Arthrex implementation webpage and Arthrex Q&As; Director_PTABDecision_Review@uspto.gov (for notifications copying counsel); Director_Review_Suggestions@uspto.gov (public feedback); Trials@uspto.gov (case-specific questions and general Arthrex-related questions); ptab statistics pages and fast-track program pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should use the listed USPTO webpages and email addresses for submitting notifications, obtaining information, and providing feedback on procedures; consult PTAB statistics and special studies (e.g., Motion to Amend study, Orange book/biologics study) for empirical context when advising clients.
